questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Bhutan?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Bhutan?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Bhutan on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bhutan article.

questions.proof: The country is bordered on the south by the Republic of India and on the north by China.

questions.prompt: Which country has the capital city Thimphu?

hints.nudge: Every country has one capital city. Find the city in the question on a map, then see which country it sits in.
hints.whereToLook: Look on the Atlas: find the city, then see which country it sits in.

questions.proof: The capital city of Bhutan is Thimphu.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Bhutan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Bhutan on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Bhutan about 38,394 square kilometres; East Timor about 14,919 square kilometres; Singapore about 719 square kilometres; Palau about 466 square kilometres.
